atlas-tw.0103: The Big Four recruit through Chinese-language campus fairs and portals; no page we read states a language level for audit graduates.
atlas-tw.0104: German companies in Taiwan look for bilingual staff who can at least communicate in English; graduates often speak English but often only passively, and returning graduates from abroad are in high demand.
atlas-tw.0105: TSMC runs its campus and internship application on its own portal and recruits at Taiwanese universities; English-only roles are mostly in semiconductor engineering and foreign firms, in our reading, and no page we read states a level.
atlas-tw.0106: In 2024 new entrants earned NT$37,000 a month on average (university graduates NT$34,000, graduate school NT$52,000), 18.7% of them started at the basic wage of NT$27,470, and of the 2023 entrants still employed in December 2024, pay had risen 15.7%.
atlas-tw.0107: The overall unemployment rate was 3.32% in August 2026 (seasonally adjusted) and 3.41% unadjusted, with 11.74% among 15- to 24-year-olds; we found no figure for graduates alone.
atlas-tw.0108: Resident visa for study and ARC
atlas-tw.0109: Apply for the resident visa at a Taipei office before travelling, then register for an Alien Resident Certificate within 30 days of arrival. Taiwan does not take apostilles: diplomas need consular legalisation by the Taipei office.
atlas-tw.0110: With a student work permit you may work 20 hours a week in term and without limit in official vacations. Public health insurance starts after six months.
atlas-tw.0112: Internships for students of foreign universities
atlas-tw.0113: The company obtains economy-ministry approval; you need at least one completed semester, and the internship must pay at least the minimum wage, 40 hours a week at most, with accident cover. Up to 180 days on a visitor visa, longer on a resident visa.
atlas-tw.0117: Graduates of Taiwanese universities can stay up to two years to look for work and may work freely meanwhile, with no work permit. Hired afterwards, a points system replaces the salary floor and the two years of experience.
atlas-tw.0119: The employer applies online; you need a master’s, or a bachelor’s plus two years of experience (waived for graduates of a top-1,500 university). The company needs NT$5 million of capital or NT$10 million of turnover, unless it is in a science park or a certified start-up.
atlas-tw.0122: An open work permit, resident visa, ARC and re-entry permit in one, for one to three years, not tied to an employer. Eligible with a monthly income of NT$160,000 in the last three years or merit criteria in ten fields; permanent residence after three years.
atlas-tw.0123: Unpaid research visits up to 180 days use a visitor visa; paid academic posts need ministry approval and a resident visa, with public health cover from day one.
atlas-tw.0124: MOE Taiwan Scholarships and Academia Sinica’s TIGP fund PhDs; PhDs from Taiwan can be hired as post-docs without the experience rule and can apply straight for the Gold Card.
atlas-tw.0127: Only for citizens of Germany, France, Ireland, Belgium, Poland, Czechia, the Netherlands, Slovakia, Austria, Hungary and Luxembourg, aged 18 to 30: 180 days, extendable once by 180. Italy has no agreement.
atlas-tw.0128: British citizens aged 18 to 30 share 1,000 places a year: 180 days, extendable once by 180, with work allowed.
atlas-tw.0129: EU and UK citizens visit up to 90 days with no work; fill in the Taiwan Arrival Card within three days before arriving. EU citizens cannot extend; British citizens can, by 90 days.
atlas-tw.0130: Workers need two documents: a work permit from the Ministry of Labor and a resident visa from the Bureau of Consular Affairs, which leads to the resident certificate (ARC).
atlas-tw.0131: A rent deposit is capped at 2 months’ rent by law; before signing, get the landlord’s explicit consent to register the address for your ARC.
atlas-tw.0132: Tell the National Immigration Agency within 30 days of any change of address or employer, or face a fine of NT$2,000 to NT$10,000.
atlas-tw.0133: Apply to the National Immigration Agency for the ARC within 30 days of entering on a resident visa. On a single-entry visa, do not leave Taiwan before collecting the card: leaving cancels the visa. The card’s chip includes a multiple re-entry permit.
atlas-tw.0134: Your Uniform ID number (one letter and nine digits, the same format as Taiwanese citizens) is printed on the ARC and used for tax, bank, health care, leases and utilities; without an ARC you can ask the agency for a paper certificate (NT$100).
atlas-tw.0135: Employees are covered by National Health Insurance and labour insurance from day one; students and people not working wait 6 months, during which they need private international cover of at least €100,000.
atlas-tw.0136: Banks want your passport, the ARC (ideally valid 6 months or more), a personal seal (chop) and a Taiwanese SIM in your name; Chunghwa Post opens basic accounts even with a passport and the UI number certificate.
atlas-tw.0137: You may renew the ARC from 3 months before it expires.
atlas-tw.0138: An Italian car licence converts without tests after 6 months with an ARC, but only for cars and mopeds up to 50cc, not 125–150cc scooters.
atlas-tw.0139: Apply for the ARC within 30 days of arrival: late applications are fined up to NT$50,000 and can bring an entry ban.
atlas-tw.0140: On a single-entry resident visa, do not leave Taiwan before collecting the ARC card, or the visa is void.
atlas-tw.0141: Report a change of address or employer within 30 days.
atlas-tw.0142: Working without a permit as a student means fines of NT$30,000 to 150,000 and expulsion.
atlas-tw.0143: A converted Italian licence covers cars and 50cc mopeds only, not 125cc scooters.
atlas-tw.0144: Whether Italy and Taiwan are negotiating a working-holiday agreement.
atlas-tw.0145: Taiwan has announced a digital nomad visa of six months to two years; consulates do not yet take applications.
atlas-tw.0146: How self-employed income counts towards the Gold Card’s NT$160,000 threshold.
